To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scale-dependent cosmology can explain the observed Hubble diagram, and that the value of Ω0 is an unknown function of the red shift.

(i) the linear Hubble law remains valid in this model, (ii) this model can account for the fact that the value of Ω0 is an increase function of the red-shift, (iii) the red-shift-luminosity distance relation is scale-dependent and can be approximated by a power law for small red-shifts, and (iv) the mass density is an increasing function for small red-shift.

(a) for nearby objects (z<<1), the Hubble diagram remains linear in scale-dependent cosmology; (b) for large redshift, scale-dependent cosmology is consistent with the observed redshift-luminosity relation and the observed behavior of Ω0 as a function of z.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to cosmology in which the universe is viewed as being embedded in a highly dense shell with a center of underdense matter.
the study of the observational consequences of a new scale-dependent cosmological theory.
the study of the observational consequences of the scale-dependent cosmological models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scale-dependent model provides an alternative to the standard cosmological model.
the Hubble law is valid for nearby objects, but not for distant ones.
the scale-dependent cosmological models are consistent with the observational data and that they are not ruled out by any of the observational constraints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hubble constant and the mass density are both functions of the scale, i.e., they are scale-dependent.
the model provides a possible explanation of the observed Hubble diagram and mass density distribution without invoking the cosmological constant.
the scale-dependent model can explain the Hubble diagram and the evolution of mass density as a result of the inhomogeneity of our universe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scale-dependent cosmologies may be able to explain the observed redshift-distance relation without the need of dark energy.
the scale dependence of the gravitational constant is a natural consequence of a scale-dependent cosmological constant and the Hubble law remains unchanged for nearby objects.
the universe may be inhomogeneous on large scales and yet the Hubble diagram may remain valid.
